title: 'I want to answer the question of how do you start a business that directly funds higher quality education in low income neighborhoods?'
summary: Josh Bell — Goodreads reader — publishes a 5-star review comparing Incorruptible to Muhammad Yunus's Banker to the Poor as sharing an outlook of using the economic system as a platform for change. Zeros in on Zita Cobb's Shorefast as the case study that stuck, and says the book brought him one step closer to answering how to start a business that funds higher-quality education in low-income neighborhoods.
blockquote: I'm inspired. After finishing this book I want to actively seek to bring these lessons, not only into my own life, but spread them to others as much as possible.
